title: Learning Design & Training Product Manager
description: Location: Bracknell, UK (hybrid, 2 days per week in office) | Type: Full-time, 37.5 hour Reports to: Head of Portfolio The role in brief Most learning designers build courses. In this role, you will own them. As our Instructional Design & Training Products Manager, you will take a portfolio of professional training products from first idea to finished, quality-assured release, and keep them at their best for as long as they are in use. The training you build is used by aviation (civil and defence) professionals whose decisions keep people safe, so getting it right matters. You will work alongside some of the most respected subject matter experts in aviation safety, helping them turn deep technical knowledge into learning that is clear, engaging and works in the classroom, online and in blended formats. You will have real influence over how we design, develop and quality-assure our training, including how we use AI to do it better. If you have a background in learning design or training product development, a sharp eye for quality, and want to see your work make a visible difference, we would like to hear from you. Why this role matters This role owns the full lifecycle of a defined segment of our training and consulting portfolio. You will be the bridge between our subject matter experts and the wider business – sales, marketing and delivery – making sure every product is high-quality, ISO-compliant and commercially sound. Just as importantly, you will help make our portfolio more scalable, so that great products no longer depend on SMEs doing all of the development themselves. What you will do Own the product lifecycle: take a defined set of training and consulting products through design, development, QA, release and maintenance, delivering against timelines, budgets, quality standards and commercial goals. Identify learning needs: use training needs and gap analysis, customer insight and delivery feedback to shape new products and refresh and improve existing ones. Lead learning design with SMEs: turn expert knowledge into clear learning objectives, specifications, storyboards and design documentation. Shape new products: work with Business Development and SMEs to define market needs, build the case for new products and position them for sale. Create high-quality materials: presentations, workbooks, facilitator guides, lesson plans, marketing collateral and digital content. Champion quality: run QA, proofreading, brand, IP and publication checks before anything is released. Keep products current: manage version control, maintenance cycles and product KPIs. Improve the learner experience: raise the standard of design and usability across classroom, virtual and blended formats. Work smarter with AI: use AI tools to speed up development and reduce SME drafting time. What you will bring At least 2 years’ experience in training product development, instructional or learning design, or L&D content development. A track record of designing professional training materials for classroom, virtual or blended delivery. A solid grounding in learning design principles (for example ADDIE) and in training needs and gap analysis. A strong eye for quality and detail – you notice what others miss, from a weak learning objective to an inconsistent heading. Strong project management skills, and the ability to juggle several products, deadlines and stakeholders at once. Confidence working with subject matter experts: asking the right questions, challenging constructively, and turning expertise into effective learning. Advanced skills in PowerPoint, Word, Excel and Adobe Acrobat. Excellent written English, to publication standard. Nice to have Experience in aviation, defence or another safety-critical or regulated industry. E-learning or blended learning development experience. A recognised L&D or instructional design qualification. An understanding of IP and contract frameworks. Experience using AI in content development. What success looks like 90% or more of product milestones delivered on time. 100% of releases meet QA, brand and IP standards. A 40% reduction in SME effort on repeatable development tasks. Fewer maintenance requests and releases each year. AI used effectively across the development process. Positive feedback from stakeholders and learners on usability and quality. Join Baines Simmons Baines Simmons builds the competence behind aerospace and defence safety. For 25 years we have delivered expert, approachable training and consulting to civil and military aviation organisations worldwide: more than 750 organisations served, over 200,000 professionals trained, and 40 or more regulatory authorities advised. We work as one with our clients, sharing serious know-how, rigour and expertise. Across every sector, and alongside global regulators, we help organisations continuously improve safety, airworthiness and compliance. We go beyond helping them comply with regulations; we empower them to excel in operational and safety performance. We look for curiosity, passion, leadership and impact. Our people do not just advise on safety. They change how clients manage it. If you want your work to make a measurable difference to aviation safety, we would like to hear from you. One organisation, four brands Baines Simmons is one of four TrustFlight brands. TrustFlight is the Aerospace Safety Intelligence Platform, building the technology that helps aviation operate safely and stay compliant. Redline Assured Security delivers government-standard aviation security, and Kenyon International delivers crisis management and response. Each brand keeps its own name, heritage and team. Together we share one platform, one set of values and one purpose: closing the gaps between disconnected tools and providers, because those gaps are where risk accumulates. Working at Baines Simmons means your expertise connects to all four . Why people stay We believe people do their best work when they have the freedom to do their job without too many rules and barriers getting in the way. Our culture is built on empowerment and trust: we hire good people and expect them to make the right calls for the customer, company, and themselves. Transforming an industry means our people have to keep learning. We earn our clients' confidence by being honest and dependable with each other, and that includes caring about the important things in life outside of work. Our offices in the UK, Canada, the US and Jersey are where teams meet to collaborate and plan. People who deliver earn more say in how their career develops, from the path they take to the flexibility they need. If you want to make a real difference to safety, this is the place to be. How we work with AI TrustFlight is an AI-first organisation, and we provide AI training where it is appropriate for your role. In this role that means using AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Copilot and Gamma) to draft and structure content, accelerate documentation and reports, and support knowledge management, while critically reviewing and refining every AI-generated output for accuracy, clarity and professional quality. You will design and apply AI-enabled workflows that make product development faster and more consistent, look for new places to integrate AI into our processes, and share what works with the team. You will complete our AI fluency onboarding within your first 30 days and spend four hours a month experimenting with AI tools and building your skills. Where and how you will work Working hours: 37.5 hours per week, core hours 09:00–17:00 Work pattern: Hybrid, 2 days per week in our Bracknell office Travel: Occasional travel as required On-call or shift work: None Screening or clearance: Criminal record check required What we offer Competitive salary of £38,000 to £44,000 Generous holiday allowance Company pension contribution Healthcare cover for everyone, including dental and optical Support for personal career development Flexible working arranged with your manager Ready to apply? Send us your CV. We would also love a short cover letter telling us about a training product you designed and are proud of: what the need was, how you approached it, and what difference it made. title: Graduate Mechanical Design Engineer
description: Company NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there. Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris. Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators. Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it. Hiring now We are hiring as soon as possible. This role is for someone who has already graduated, or who will complete their degree in time to start with us very soon. We are not able to consider final-year students who graduate in summer 2027 or later, and this is not a graduate scheme with a fixed annual intake. Role Overview This is a first full-time engineering role on the NEO-1 satellite. You will design satellite hardware and help keep the satellite's full CAD assembly organised as the design matures, learning from our lead designer and working in a small, multidisciplinary team. You will take ownership of real parts early, translate requirements into manufacturable designs and support their validation through prototyping and environmental testing. Key Responsibilities Design and develop mechanical hardware for the satellite, such as brackets, panels, component mounts, thermal-control hardware and cable and harness routing, with guidance from the lead designer. Work in the satellite's large 3D CAD assembly alongside the wider design team, learning how to keep interfaces, configurations and revisions in step as several designers work in the same model. Support assembly configuration, PLM data (3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX') or similar), bills of materials and engineering change control (ECO/ECR/ECN), so that models, drawings and interfaces stay consistent as changes are released. Run interference and clash checks and help maintain the digital mock-up, working with each subsystem owner to allocate space and resolve conflicts. Produce dimensioned, manufacturing-ready drawings using GD&T, with review from senior engineers. Support design reviews (PDR and CDR) and qualification, working with structural and thermal engineers. Work with manufacturers and suppliers to make designs easier to build, and to balance cost, mass and reliability. Support prototype builds, integration and environmental test campaigns, iterating designs based on results. Collaborate with electrical, software, systems and thermal engineers to integrate mechanical components into the satellite platform. Required Skills & Experience Bachelor's or master's degree in mechanical, aerospace or a related engineering discipline, completed or completing very soon. Hands-on 3D CAD skills from university projects, a placement or an internship (SolidWorks preferred; CATIA, NX or Creo also considered). Working knowledge of GD&T and experience producing engineering drawings, including from coursework or a team project. Solid grounding in mechanical design principles, materials and thermal management, with a working understanding of structural mechanics. Evidence of designing, building and testing something real, such as a placement project, Formula Student, a UAV, or a rocketry or satellite team, including troubleshooting and iteration. Clear communicator who is comfortable explaining and defending design decisions, and open to feedback and challenge in a fast-moving team. Preferred Experience A placement, internship or year in industry in aerospace, space, motorsport or another high-reliability field. Experience of several people working in one CAD assembly, for example in a Formula Student or university team, including how files and revisions were controlled. Exposure to PLM or PDM systems (for example 3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX'), Windchill, Teamcenter, ENOVIA or SolidWorks PDM) or to formal engineering change processes (ECO/ECR/ECN). Experience of design reviews, documented requirements and standards. Satellite, CubeSat or rocketry project experience, including hardware that has launched. Basic FEA familiarity and exposure to manufacturing processes. Why NewOrbit Space? Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO. Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology. Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success. Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups. Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week. Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Product Engineer
description: Hi 👋 I’m Rich Ashworth, Director of Engineering at hyperexponential. I lead the Model Authoring value stream that owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models. An actuary might start with an Excel rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved, and is pricing live business. Our job is to turn that into an exceptional user experience and make every step of that credible enough to trust. I'm hiring a Staff Product Engineer to help set our technical direction and build the next version of our products. It's an individual contributor role, but influence is a huge part of it: the standards the pods work to, the shared enablers underneath the product, and the interfaces where our problems meet other teams'. You’ll be hands-on where the risk is highest. There's no established playbook for any of this, but there’s an incredible opportunity in front of us. If this sounds like a role that would excite you, I'd love to hear from you. About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the Model Authoring team Model Authoring owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models: the model developer experience and our actuarial agent. An actuary might start with an Excel-based rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved and is pricing live business. Our job is to make every step of that credible enough to trust. The team is distributed across our Warsaw and London offices. As the Staff Product Engineer, you will help set the team's technical direction. This is an individual contributor role, but influence is a large part of it: you'll help define the standards the team works to, raise the technical bar across pods, and own the interfaces where our problems meet those of teams elsewhere in Technology. You'll be expected to move fast and start shaping technical conversations early. We work in an AI-native way, and you'll help define and evolve what that means here. What you'll be doing Establish a set of engineering standards across the Model Authoring pods. The standards are documented and actively referenced in code review, with new pod work conforming by default. Set and own the technical direction for the team's shared enablers, including how we represent and persist models, the model registry, secure context access, and shared agentic infrastructure. Establish the technical interfaces between Model Authoring and other parts of the business. Dependencies with other teams are agreed, documented, and progressing without needing to be brokered by someone else. Work hands-on on the hardest problems in the stream. This is not an advisory role: we would expect you in the code where the risk is highest. Help define how we work in an AI-native way. Which parts of model development and of our own engineering we hand to agents, what stays human, and what evidence we need before trusting either. Visibly lift the engineers around you. You're sought out for design input across pods, and there's at least one engineer whose growth is clearly attributable to your support. What you'll need to have done Worked in an AI-native environment, and genuinely want to keep doing so. You've used AI or agentic tools in your own engineering workflow, introduced or experimented with them, and have a real view on what's worked and what hasn't. Been product-focused rather than purely technical. You understand who your users are, where their pain points are, and how your technical decisions connect to commercial outcomes. Set technical direction while navigating genuine ambiguity. A proven track record of owning architecture in a domain with no established playbook, and making clear calls on imperfect information rather than deferring them. Owned a significant technical challenge or service end to end, with the depth to walk through it in detail - the trade-offs, the contracts, the things you'd do differently. Influenced across teams. You can hold a position under challenge, genuinely listen to pushback, and persuade others - not just present your own view and hope it lands. Worked effectively across distributed teams - this role spans our Warsaw and London offices, so you'll need to be comfortable building relationships and influence across both. You're unlikely to thrive here if You'd rather focus purely on the technical problem than get close to users, customer pain points, and the commercial implications of what you build. You're not comfortable setting technical direction in ambiguity, or you'd rather wait for an established playbook than make a call on imperfect information. You're not excited about helping define what the future of software engineering looks like and are prepared to embrace tooling and new ways of working to support this. If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us. Compensation At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. title: GRC Engineer
description: A little about us incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime. The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously. We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join. The role in one line Being a GRC Engineer at incident.io means turning compliance from spreadsheets and screenshots into something that just runs, so “can you prove it?” gets answered before anyone asks. What that looks like day to day As a GRC Engineer at incident.io , you own how we prove we’re doing the right thing: our compliance programme, our customer security questionnaires, and the evidence behind both. One day you’re building an AI workflow that drafts questionnaire answers, the next you’re pushing our ISO 27001 work forward, the next you’re telling the product team what makes GRC painful. Our GRC programme is young, and Slack is our system of record. You’ll make it scale, using AI-powered tooling and workflows to take the toil out of audits, evidence collection and customer questions. title: Data Center Architect
description: Role Profile Job Title: Data Centre Architect Reports to: Head of Data Centre Development Location: UK hybrid Company Overview: Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built. We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments. We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software. As we scale, we’re building this organisation from the ground up. We’re looking for people who’d rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of team you’ve previously managed. This is a senior individual contributor role with authority to sign off technical schedules, working with cluster and network architects, NVIDIA and other OEM engineers, colocation provider engineering and sales teams, and the internal Procurement, Legal, Finance and Site Operations teams. What You’ll Do You will be the single technical authority between our GPU-as-a-service business and the colocation providers that host our NVIDIA clusters. You turn cluster architecture and OEM requirements into a precise, contractable statement of work (SOW) for the data centre white space, then hold the provider to it through design, installation and acceptance. We are growing from tens of megawatts to hundreds, on rack-scale liquid-cooled platforms at 130 kW per rack and rising to 200 kW and beyond. Mistakes in power, cooling or fibre specification show up as stranded capacity, delayed cluster delivery and disputes, so the role carries real commercial weight. Key Responsibilities Technical negotiation with colocation providers Lead technical due diligence on candidate sites: power availability and energisation dates, redundancy topology, liquid-cooling capability, floor loading, rack logistics, fibre and meet-me access. Negotiate the technical schedules of the colocation agreement with commercial and legal: capacity and density commitments, power and cooling SLAs, temperature and flow envelopes, metering, expansion rights, change control and remedies. Challenge provider claims with evidence: single-line diagrams, P&IDs, load-bank and commissioning records, reference customers. Specification & SOW Work with cluster architects and OEMs (NVIDIA first) to capture rack, power, cooling, network and layout requirements, and keep them current across product generations. Write and own the technical SOW for white-space fitout: containment and cooling interfaces, power distribution to rack, structured cabling and pathways, rack and POD layout, security zoning, labelling and records. Define clear scope boundaries and responsibilities between us, the colocation provider, OEMs and installation contractors, with no gaps and no overlaps. Maintain a requirements baseline with traceability from OEM document, to SOW clause, to acceptance test. Design, installation & acceptance Review provider and contractor designs, shop drawings and method statements against the SOW; run design reviews and close findings. Define acceptance: factory and site tests, liquid flush and cleanliness, power quality, thermal performance at full load, fibre loss, burn-in, and the evidence pack needed for each gate. Attend key witness tests and sign off, or reject, completion of each phase before hardware is energised. Manage technical change requests and variations, and advise on cost and schedule impact. Knowledge & standards Build reusable reference designs, SOW templates and a site-scoring framework so each new deployment starts from a proven baseline. Track the roadmap: higher rack densities, 800 VDC distribution, new cooling classes and optics, and tell the business early what it means for sites already contracted. Deliverables You Own: Site technical assessment: Scored, evidence-based report per candidate site, comparable across providers, with risks and mitigations. Technical schedules to the colocation agreement: Measurable commitments, tested in acceptance, with remedies agreed by legal. Cluster white-space SOW: Complete enough that a contractor can price and build without asking us questions; traceable to OEM requirements. Reference designs and layouts: Rack, row and POD layouts, power and cooling single-line and P&ID level interfaces, fibre pathways and densities. Acceptance test plan and evidence pack: Pass and fail criteria set before work starts; signed results per gate. Requirements baseline and change log: One current version of the truth, with every variation recorded and costed. Risk and issues register: Technical risks to schedule and capacity, with owners and dates. Working Relationships: Cluster and network architects: You translate their cluster design into facility requirements, and they rely on you to say what a site can and cannot carry. OEMs, mainly NVIDIA: You are the facility-side counterpart; you obtain, interpret and challenge site-requirement documents. Colocation providers: Day-to-day technical counterpart through negotiation, build and acceptance. Procurement, legal and finance: You provide the technical substance of commercial terms and the impact of variations. Site operations and deployment teams: You hand over a clean specification and acceptance evidence, and take back lessons learned. What You Bring: 8 or more years in data centre design, delivery or technical consulting, including at least 3 years on high-density (50 kW per rack or more) or liquid-cooled deployments. Direct experience writing or reviewing technical specifications and SOWs for white-space fitout, and managing contractors against them to acceptance. Strong working knowledge of data centre power: MV and LV distribution, UPS and generator topologies, redundancy models (N+1, 2N, distributed), busway and rack power, metering and power quality. Strong working knowledge of cooling: direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility and technology loops, warm-water and dry-cooler designs, fluid quality and flushing, leak detection and containment. Working knowledge of structured cabling and pathways for large GPU fabrics (single-mode optics, high fibre counts, InfiniBand and Ethernet physical layers), and of rack and POD layouts. Familiarity with NVIDIA rack-scale platforms (GB200 or GB300 class, or later) and their facility requirements, and the ability to read OEM site-requirement documents critically. Proven ability to run technical negotiations with colocation or construction counterparties, and to explain trade-offs to commercial, legal and executive audiences. Command of standards such as EN 50600 and the Uptime Tier framework, ASHRAE TC 9.9 liquid-cooling guidance, and commissioning practice (levels 1 to 5). Excellent written communication: you produce clear, unambiguous contract-grade documents. Preferred Skills (Nice to Have): Experience at a hyperscaler, neocloud or colocation provider on the operator or customer side. Experience with 800 VDC or other DC distribution, large battery storage, or power smoothing for AI load swings. Chartered engineer status or equivalent; recognised data centre credentials (for example CDCP, CDFOM, Uptime ATD or AOS). Familiarity with BIM, digital-twin tools and requirements-management tools. Willingness to travel up to 30% to sites in the UK, Europe and the US. Success Measures: First 90 days: Audit current colocation contracts and SOWs and list technical gaps; publish a requirements baseline for the current NVIDIA platform; take over technical lead on one live negotiation; agree the site-scoring framework with the cluster architects. 6 months: One complete SOW issued and priced with no material scope disputes; acceptance plan agreed with the provider before build starts; reusable SOW template adopted by the team. 12 months: Every new site contracted on the template with traceable requirements; clusters accepted on schedule with no facility-caused performance issues; fewer late variations and a measurable cut in time from site shortlist to signed technical schedule. Qualities we look for: Set the standard: Every single day, you spot opportunities to constructively shake things up. Inspire the change: There’s no blueprint for the future. You’ll embrace challenges and change. You’re real and you’re true to yourself: We cherish and celebrate diversity so you’ll feel right at home whoever you are and whoever you’re talking to, you treat everyone the same. Get stuck in: You’d rather be building than overseeing. Our strategy will keep evolving, and so will you — attitude and adaptability matter more to us than a fixed playbook or a big team behind you. Package & Process: Employment type: Full-time, permanent. Travel: Up to 30%. Interview process: Talent Screening > Hiring Manager Screen > Technical Interview > Final with the Head of Data Centre Development. The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows. We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software. Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it. The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too. We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else. What you'll own Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself. Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached. Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it. The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them. What we're looking for You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar. Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start. Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it. A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that. In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done. Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting. Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV. How we work There are five things we care about deeply: Reason from the ground up Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts. Speed begets speed We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin. Take ownership Do not wait for permission to do things. Brutal honesty If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to. Truly excellent customer service Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster. This role is probably not for you if You'd rather write specs and hand tickets to engineers than build the thing yourself; You prefer close management of your responsibilities; You are risk-averse; You want a 9-5; You take yourself too seriously; You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact Salary £90k - £120k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
description: What Quadrants is Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research. The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton. It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public. The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast. The role You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap. Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further. It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows. The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX. Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime. What you’ll own API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches. IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality. Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform. Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking. Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works. The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction. Who you are You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward. The ground that judgment stands on: GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus. Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them. Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability. And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term). What great looks like People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder. What we’re uncompromising about How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound. That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it. Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are. title: ML Compiler & System
description: What Quadrants is Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research. The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton. It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public. The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast. The role You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap. Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further. It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows. The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX. What you’ll own API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches. IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality. Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform. Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking. Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works. The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction. Who you are You reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward. The ground that judgment stands on: GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus. Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them. Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability. And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term). What great looks like People adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder. What we’re uncompromising about How you work is up to you. What matters is that your ownership grows over time: blind spots shrink, the parts you can vouch for expand, technical debt goes down, the core stays sound. That takes treating understanding as real work, not overhead. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it. Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners. You are. What you'll do Lead, coach, and develop a lean team of IT engineers - setting priorities, unblocking their hardest problems, and stepping in hands-on for complex or escalated issues. Own Okta identity and access management for the business: the lifecycle, integrations, and day-to-day administration that keep joiners, movers, and leavers secure and frictionless. Own macOS and Apple device management and endpoint tooling across the business, in a way that's secure by default and low-friction for Paddlers. Drive the adoption of data, automation, and AI across IT operations - identifying where tooling and agents can remove manual toil, speed up support, and evolve how the team operates. Set and own IT's operating rhythm: support tooling, SLAs, and the metrics that show whether the function is improving. Manage the IT budget and vendor portfolio - evaluating spend, negotiating commercial terms, ensuring that we’re operating efficiently and running a SaaS estate that spans across multiple departments. Implement and maintain baseline security and resilience practices for IT-owned systems (CIS Benchmarks, patching, disaster recovery), partnering closely with the wider Security team on anything that crosses into security engineering. title: Partnerships Lead, UK&I
description: Build something monumental for Healthcare! At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care. We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you! About the Role We are looking for an ambitious, commercially driven Partnerships Lead to build and scale Tandem Health's strategic partnerships across the UK. You will play a key role in accelerating our growth by identifying and securing high-impact partnerships across the healthcare ecosystem, including NHS organisations, private healthcare providers, hospital groups and healthtech platforms. You'll own the full partnership lifecycle, from identifying opportunities and building senior relationships through to negotiating agreements, launching partnerships and driving commercial value. Working closely with our commercial, product and leadership teams, you'll help unlock new routes to market, expand our distribution and establish Tandem as a leading AI partner to UK healthcare. What You Will Do Own and execute Tandem's UK partnerships strategy, identifying the relationships and channels that will have the greatest impact on our growth. Identify and secure strategic partnerships across the UK healthcare ecosystem, including NHS organisations, private healthcare providers, hospital groups and specialist clinic networks. Develop relationships with EHR/EMR providers, digital health platforms and complementary technology businesses to unlock new distribution and integration opportunities. Originate and manage partnership opportunities end-to-end, from initial outreach and business development through to commercial negotiations, contracting and launch. Develop compelling partnership propositions and commercial models that create value for both Tandem and its partners. Drive tangible outcomes from partnerships, including revenue generation, customer acquisition, clinician adoption and market expansion. Work closely with sales, product, project delivery, medical operations and marketing teams to ensure successful implementation and maximise the value of strategic partnerships. Represent Tandem at industry events and conferences, building our profile and network across the UK healthcare market. Monitor market developments and identify new opportunities to strengthen Tandem's competitive position and accelerate growth. What You Bring Proven experience in strategic partnerships, ideally within healthcare, healthtech or enterprise technology. Strong understanding of the UK healthcare landscape, including NHS structures, private healthcare and the wider digital health ecosystem. An established network of relevant industry contacts, with the ability to build credibility and influence senior decision-makers. Demonstrable track record of originating and closing complex, high-value commercial partnerships. Experience developing partnership strategies, identifying new routes to market and creating scalable commercial opportunities. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators. We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale. In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership. We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide. Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems. At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception. The Role We're hiring a Senior Data Engineer . Data sits at the core of what tem does. Our time-series data is the spine that runs from pricing through to billing: every transaction depends on it working. You'll be working across a genuinely varied set of workloads: textual data, time-series data, and event streams, each with its own ingestion and reliability challenges, including TSDS. You'll join our Data Service team of 4, owning the design, reliability, and recovery strategy of specific ingestion pipelines and systems end-to-end. This is an individual contributor role: no team to manage, full ownership of the work you do. description: About Seamflow Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files. Where we are: Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed , co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze. Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists. The team Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further. The role A Product Engineer owns the surfaces people actually work in. A coordinator planning a month of inspections across a fleet of auditors. A reviewer signing off on a technical file. These are dense, stateful workflows where the interface carries real consequences, and where the person using it has done the job for twenty years and will know immediately if the software doesn't understand it. You own product surface end to end: the interface, the backend that supports it, and the data model underneath. Every customer runs the work differently, so there's no template to fall back on. You decide what the right thing to build is, build it, and are the one who hears about it when it's wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week. What we're looking for We care far more about raw engineering strength than about matching a list of technologies. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, C++ or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, speed and standards are not. What we're actually screening for: You've built something hard and put it in front of real users. Not a prototype, not a course project. Something that ran, broke, and got fixed. You build genuinely good interfaces , and you can go as deep on the backend as the feature requires. You can hold a complicated workflow in your head and find the version of it that's simple enough to ship. Speed with taste. You ship fast, and you're opinionated about what not to build. You go to the source. You'll read the customer's actual documents, join the actual call, and look at hundreds of real outputs. Signals we like, none of them required: founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, early engineer at a startup with a serious engineering culture, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup, design sense you can defend, open source you genuinely maintain. AI at our foundation, cyber risk at our core. We don't just use AI, we shape it. Built on AI from day one. Artificial intelligence has been part of our strategy since the beginning, blended with deep cybersecurity and insurance expertise and backed by rigorous testing. Trusted by more than 100 clients, including 75% of the top 40 European and US cyber insurance carriers and 70% of the top ten reinsurance brokers. Backed for global growth. In 2025 Spectrum Equity joined some of CyberCube’s financial partners as a new cornerstone investor, accelerating our global growth and fueling innovation across our end-to-end cyber risk analytics for the insurance industry. A truly global team across San Francisco, New York, London, and Tallinn. A culture of collaboration, openness, intellectual rigor, and ownership for excellence. People at the forefront. We encourage CyberCubers to challenge themselves, push boundaries, and do the best work of their careers. The Impact You Will Make Work in a team of cyber threat analysts, economists, data scientists, actuaries and risk modelers to develop insights, scores, and features for a suite of products delivering cyber risk analytics to the (re)insurance industry Own CyberCube's point of view on technology risk including factors such as: Offensive capabilities and trends among threat actor classes, and validating CyberCube models against observed real-world events, Security hygiene standards (e.g. NIST CSF, CIS) and mitigations for companies to lower their potential likelihood and/or impact of events, and Technology adoption and trends including the adoption, reliance on and governance of artificial intelligence … translating these factors into the assumptions and scenarios that drive risk models – especially where historical data is limited Own the scenario and "event family" library for cyber catastrophe modeling, including emerging AI-driven scenarios Own the assumptions register and expert-judgment governance: the documented, client-defensible rationale for modeling choices that are not purely data-driven Present CyberCube methodology, threat landscape and emerging risk trends to clients and prospects and engage in strategic dialogue with key stakeholders as one of CyberCube's key voices and thought leaders on technology risk. Be able to differentiate when speaking with varying technical backgrounds and seniority (e.g. analyst to C-Suite) Engage in cross functional collaboration with stakeholders from engineering, product title: Senior Manager, Creator Partnerships & Social Commerce
description: Build, Scale & Operate Leading DTC Brands alongside A-Players Maneuver Marketing Our Vision, Mission & Success are fuelled by our commitment to be a driving force of positive change to the health of everyday consumers, providing conscious, high-quality & innovative supplement products. In just 5 years, we kicked off our own DTC Health & Wellness brand from scratch and scaled it to USD$100M+ in annual sales, serving more than 3,000,000 customers worldwide with an average of 4,000 daily orders across 9 SKUs. These results caught the attention of The Financial Times , as they ranked us among APACs top High-Growth Companies. We have also been awarded 2nd place on the E50 Awards , jointly organised by The Business Times and KPMG in Singapore. This is just the beginning of our journey, and you could be part of the next stage of our growth! Your Next Role We are looking for a strategic, commercially minded and highly organized Senior Manager, Creator Partnerships & Social Commerce to lead and scale our creator marketing capability. You will own the end-to-end creator strategy and drive implementation for two women’s health brands. One brand offers supplements that help with symptoms and root causes, and the other offers supplements that support one’s lifestyle habits and addresses nutritional gaps. Leading a team of two associates who execute the seeding program, you will upgrade and refine our current strategy to build a reliable community of high-quality creator partnerships that strengthen our organic presence, generate commercially valuable content and support our paid media performance. This is a hands-on management role. You will set the strategy and performance targets, develop the team, improve our systems and processes, and remain directly involved in high-value partnerships and campaign decisions. The ideal candidate combines strong creator marketing instincts with operational discipline, commercial judgment and a clear understanding of how creator content can be transformed into effective paid advertising. What You’ll Do 1. Own the Creator Strategy Across Both Brands Own creator strategy for two women's health brands across two distinct motions: an established seeding program producing content at volume, and a new TikTok Shop affiliate program built for direct sales. Scope is deliberately asymmetric. Seeding covers 4 flagship SKUs today, expanding to all 6 once the team's agentic workflows free the capacity. TikTok Shop launches focused on 2 products under one brand. Build creator-driven demand that shows up beyond the platform it originates on: branded search volume, Amazon and Shopify sales lift, and a content library that feeds paid media. Identify the right mix of healthcare professionals and content creators for each campaign. Establish measurable targets across outreach volume, response rates, partnership approvals, content delivery, cost efficiency and campaign performance. Monitor competitor activity, creator pricing and emerging platform trends to keep our approach relevant and competitive. Build and deploy AI workflows that increase the team's throughput - creator qualification, outreach personalization at volume, content tagging and rights tracking. We expect measurable capacity gains, not experimentation. 2. Lead and Develop the Creator Marketing Team The Meta seeding program is built and running at scale. Your associates own the day-to-day operations; your job is to consult with creative leads, sharpen briefs, run creative tests, and hold quality while the majority of your own attention goes to TikTok and affiliates. Oversee the team’s day-to-day outreach, follow-ups, creator communication, fulfilment coordination and administrative workflows. Build clear processes and operating rhythms that allow the team to manage a high volume of influencer activity accurately and efficiently. 3. Build a Scalable Creator Acquisition Pipeline Source creators across three routes: direct outreach, the TikTok Shop affiliate marketplace, and the established creator network available through our TikTok consultant. Convert the consultant's network into signed, producing partnerships rather than a list. Sustain the current output of hundreds of pieces of creator content per month across the seeding program, while building a separate affiliate creator pipeline for TikTok Shop. Assess potential partners based on audience fit, content quality, engagement, credibility, pricing and their ability to create or follow relevant trends. Develop partnerships with a strong focus on micro- and mid-sized creators, while selectively pursuing larger influencers when commercially justified. Create tailored outreach strategies for a competitive market in which larger brands may offer significantly higher creator fees. 4. Build the TikTok Shop Affiliate Program Own the TikTok Shop affiliate program for 2 products under one brand, from creator recruitment through commission structure, sample logistics and GMV performance. Set and manage commission tiers, open collaborations, targeted invites and any performance-based arrangements; decide where flat-fee and where commission-only makes sense. Own affiliate GMV as a number you're accountable for, and the unit economics behind it: cost per acquired affiliate, sample cost per producing creator, blended commission rate. Identify and develop the small number of affiliates who will drive the majority of GMV, and build repeat and exclusive arrangements with them. Work with the TikTok Affiliate Creative Strategist on creative direction. They own research, concept and brief content; you own creator supply, terms, relationship and program performance. 5. Own Campaign Execution and Creator Relationships Oversee partnerships from initial outreach and qualification through contracting, product delivery, content production, payment and performance review. Ensure creators receive clear briefs, campaign expectations, timelines and feedback. Build strong, professional relationships that encourage creators to become long-term brand advocates rather than one-off partners. Maintain an active and engaged creator community through regular updates, challenges, educational content and brand communications. Own claims compliance in creator content across both brands. Maintain the do-say/don't-say guidance creators work from, and make sure it holds at volume across seeding, affiliate and organic. Ensure FTC material-connection disclosure and platform-specific policy compliance on every partnership. TikTok Shop enforces supplement claims differently from Meta; both need to be handled correctly. 6. Turn Creator Content into Growth Assets Secure usage rights and TikTok ad authorization (Spark Ad codes) at the point of partnership, not retroactively. Establish a clear process for reviewing, categorizing and distributing creator-generated content. Evaluate content based on brand alignment, creative quality, audience relevance and potential commercial use. Work with Paid Media, Creative and Marketplace to route creator content to its highest-value use: paid social, marketplace listings, email and brand channels. Translate both organic and paid media learnings back into creator briefs so creators can produce stronger, more testable content. Supply the brand social channels with a steady flow of approved, on-brand creator content. Publishing and community management on brand-owned accounts sit with a separate role. 7. Own Tools, Vendors and Operational Excellence Manage our external partners - the TikTok consultant and content agencies - including scope, output quality, cost and the decision on when capability should move in-house. Own the influencer marketing stack end to end. We currently run SARAL; assess whether it, Modash, Lefty or an alternative best serves discovery, outreach, relationship management and reporting at our volume. Partner with Supply and Operations teams to ensure product kits are shipped accurately and on time. Oversee creator invoicing and payment workflows, ensuring submissions are accurate, approved and processed promptly. Identify bottlenecks and introduce scalable workflows, automation and documentation where appropriate. 7. Measure and Improve Performance You'll be measured on four things: TikTok Shop affiliate GMV, cost per usable content asset, branded search and marketplace lift attributable to creator activity, and content throughput against quality standard. Everything else is diagnostic. You'll manage a defined creator and sampling budget across both programs, with authority to reallocate between seeding and affiliate based on returns. Define and monitor the KPIs required to evaluate the health and commercial impact of the influencer program. Track outreach volume, open and response rates, approval rates, creator acquisition costs, content delivery, engagement, reach, conversions and return on investment. Build clear weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting for the Growth team and company leadership. Analyze performance by creator profile, product, platform, partnership structure, outreach message and content format. Maintain a structured testing roadmap covering outreach messages, incentives, creator segments and content approaches. How You’ll Succeed You combine strategic thinking with a willingness to remain close to execution. You create clarity for your team, hold people accountable and help them improve. You build a predictable pipeline of relevant creators and commercially valuable content. You use data and experimentation to improve response rates, partnership quality and return on investment. You can recognize creators who offer strong value beyond follower count alone. You build effective partnerships across Creator Marketing, Paid Media, Creative, Supply, Email Marketing and E-commerce. You introduce structure without slowing down execution. You communicate clearly, act quickly and resolve problems before they affect campaigns. You remain resourceful in a competitive market where budgets and creator expectations may not always align. You care equally about relationship quality, operational accuracy and commercial outcomes. What You Bring Required 5+ years in influencer marketing, creator partnerships or creator affiliate marketing, including at least one program you owned end to end with commercial accountability. Operator experience running a TikTok Shop or comparable creator affiliate program, with GMV or revenue you were personally accountable for. DTC or e-commerce experience in health and wellness, beauty, or another regulated consumer category. Experience managing or mentoring team members, with evidence you raised their output rather than just reviewed it. Experience managing external agencies, consultants or vendors: setting scope, holding quality, deciding when to bring work in-house. Experience structuring and negotiating both flat-fee and performance-based partnerships. Strong analytical skills and a track record of using campaign data to change decisions, not just report them. Evidence of an AI or automation workflow you built or deployed that measurably increased throughput. Be ready to walk through what it does and what it saved. Strongly preferred Ownership of brand-owned organic social channels, not only creator programs. You understand how owned content and creator content compound. Working knowledge of FTC material-connection disclosure and platform claim policy in a regulated category. You know what a creator cannot say about a supplement, and why the answer differs on TikTok and Meta. Experience collaborating with Paid Media or Creative to repurpose creator content into performance advertising, including securing ad authorization at partnership time. Hands-on with an influencer marketing platform - SARAL, Modash, Lefty or equivalent. Experience running influencer or creator programs across multiple brands or product categories. title: Account Manager - SMB
description: About Hiya At Hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective. Voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. When customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve. Hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. Our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes. This role sits in a core business area for Hiya and is focused on helping SMB and enterprise customers succeed. About the Role Hiya is growing its SMB customer base across the UK and Europe, and this role exists to ensure those customers stay, grow, and succeed. This role sits within Hiya Connect - our branded calling product. Hiya Connect Branded Call enables businesses to display their verified brand name, logo, and call reason on outbound calls, helping customers recognize trusted calls, increase answer rates, and improve engagement. As an Account Manager, SMB, you’ll own a high-volume portfolio of 300+ customers. You’ll make commercial decisions every day about how to prioritise your time, engage customers, and create growth across your book of business. The pace is fast and the portfolio is broad. Our European base is growing quickly, and this role is for someone who can work with customers in German, French or Spanish as well as English. Holding a renewal or pricing conversation in a customer’s own language builds trust faster, and at this end of the market that speed matters. This role is perfect for someone who enjoys autonomy, thrives in a high-velocity environment and wants genuine ownership of customer outcomes, with a clear path into more strategic account management as Hiya continues to scale across Europe. What You’ll Do Own a portfolio of 300+ SMB accounts across the UK and Europe, with full accountability for renewals and expansion Manage your European accounts in German, French or Spanish as well as English Triage your book daily - identify which accounts need intervention and which are healthy enough to run digitally Run proactive outreach to at-risk accounts before they become churn conversations Identify natural expansion signals - usage growth, new teams, new use cases and convert them into upsell opportunities Forecast portfolio performance and maintain accurate CRM records Surface patterns from your book of business that help Sales, Product, and Support improve how Hiya serves SMB customers Balance short-term renewal pressure with longer-term account health, making clear tradeoffs under volume What We Are Looking For 2+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a commercial SaaS role Must have - Business-level German, French or Spanish - confident holding renewal, pricing, and expansion conversations in that language Demonstrated ownership of renewals, expansions, or quota Commercial instinct - able to spot a growth opportunity, build a case for it, and close it without heavy support Clear, direct communication with customers and internal stakeholders Comfortable working independently in an environment where not every process is fully defined You’ll Likely Stand Out If You Have Experience managing SMB or Mid-Market customers Experience working across UK and European markets More than one of German, French or Spanish, or an additional European language Experience balancing personalised customer engagement with scale Exposure to conversation intelligence, caller ID, or communications technology Role details Status: Full-time Type: Hybrid Location: London, United Kingdom Travel: Up to 25% Department: Sales – Customer Success Reports to: Sr. Manager: Customer Success, UK & EU Come Work With Us! We're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. We evaluate candidates through a business lens and believe that diversity and unique viewpoints make our company stronger, more dynamic, and a great place to build a career. We've been recognized by Built In, GeekWire, Comparably, G2, Forbes, and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. At Hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. We create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. You'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. Come join us! Hiya is an equal opportunity employer. title: Senior DevSecOps Engineer

This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, platform engineering, cyber security, and defence systems engineering. The DevSecOps Engineer works alongside autonomy, software, systems, integration, and test engineers to create secure and reliable development environments and delivery pipelines that enable teams to rapidly develop, integrate, test, and deploy mission critical software. The ideal candidate has a strong software and platform engineering background combined with significant experience operating within UK defence environments. They have a strong understanding of the UK Ministry of Defence/NATO approach to DevSecOps, Secure by Design, cyber risk management, security assurance, and the delivery of software into classified and operational environments. What You’ll Do Design, build, and operate secure development and deployment infrastructure for Shield AI autonomy and defence programmes. Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines that enable rapid, repeatable, and secure delivery of autonomy and mission software. Work closely with software, autonomy, systems, cyber security, integration, and test engineers to establish development environments that support rapid engineering while meeting defence security requirements. Implement automated security controls within CI/CD pipelines, including static analysis, dependency scanning, container scanning, secrets detection, software composition analysis, vulnerability management, and policy enforcement. Significant experience delivering software or digital capabilities within UK defence or another highly regulated national security environment. Experience applying MOD security policies, security assurance processes, and technical security requirements to software intensive defence programmes. Experience developing and operating CI/CD pipelines using modern source control, build, test, artefact management, and deployment technologies. Strong understanding of Infrastructure as Code, configuration management, containerisation, and infrastructure automation Experience with technologies such as Git, GitLab or GitHub, or equivalent tooling. Desirable Qualifications Experience supporting DevSecOps, software delivery, or digital engineering activities across NATO nations or multinational defence programmes. Understanding of DevSecOps approaches, security frameworks, and software assurance practices used by other NATO nations, particularly the United States and European NATO partners.
